question: Let \(G(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-x^3}^{x^3}f(t)\,dt\), where \(x\) is any real number and \(f\) is a continuous function such that \(f(t)>1\) for all real \(t\). Then,

options.A: \(G'(0)=0\) and \(G\) has a local maximum or minimum at \(x=0\).
options.B: For any real number \(c\), the equation \(G(x)=c\) has a unique solution.
options.C: There exists a real number \(c\) such that \(G(x)=c\) has no solution.
options.D: There exists a real number \(c\) such that \(G(x)=c\) has more than one solution.
